# Feeding a sourdough starter

Let bread cool for an hour before slicing; the crumb is still setting as steam escapes. Stretch and folds during bulk fermentation build strength without heavy kneading. Hydration is the weight of water divided by the weight of flour; seventy five percent is a friendly start. Bulk fermentation is done when the dough has grown by about half and shows bubbles at the edges.

## Pitfalls

A healthy starter doubles within six hours of feeding at room temperature. A sharp lame held at a shallow angle gives the classic ear on a batard. Hydration is the weight of water divided by the weight of flour; seventy five percent is a friendly start. Whole wheat flour absorbs more water, so raise hydration when swapping it in. Shaping creates surface tension so the loaf rises up instead of spreading out.

Salt slows fermentation, so add it after the autolyse rather than at the very start. Bulk fermentation is done when the dough has grown by about half and shows bubbles at the edges.
